3

The FTP/SFTP client (ftp.html) transfers files between your computer and servers, like FileZilla. It supports SFTP (over SSH), FTPS (FTP over TLS, explicit and implicit) and plain FTP. Connections go through the local relay (see the user guide, "Network functions and the relay").

Connecting

The bar at the top connects directly: choose the protocol, enter host, port (filled in for the protocol), user and password, and click Connect.

Protocol Port Notes
SFTP (SSH) 22 password or private key (paste it into the key field); the server's host key is shown on the first connection
FTPS (explicit TLS) 21 encrypted after AUTH TLS; the usual secure FTP
FTPS (implicit TLS) 990 encrypted from the start
FTP (not encrypted) 21 passwords and files travel in clear text — use only in trusted networks

For FTPS with a self-signed server certificate, tick Accept untrusted certificates. FTP always uses passive mode; the data connections go to the same host as the control connection.

Save site stores the current settings under a name in the Sites list; a click on a site connects, ✎ loads it into the bar, × deletes it. Sites and the relay settings are kept in a connections file (KeePass database or JSON file, Save and Open… below the list).

Local and remote files

The window shows two lists: Local on the left, Remote (the server) on the right.

  • Local (Chrome/Edge on the desktop): Choose local folder… opens a folder of your computer. Double-click folders to open them, ↑ goes up. Downloads are written into this folder; folders are downloaded with their content.
  • In Firefox and on phones, local folders cannot be opened: Upload files… uploads files, and downloads go to the browser's download folder.
  • Remote: double-click a folder to open it, ↑ goes up, or type a path and press Enter; ⟳ reloads.

Click selects an entry, Ctrl+click selects several.

Transfers

  • Upload → uploads the selected local entries (folders with their content) into the current remote folder; you can also drag entries from the local list (or files from the desktop) onto the remote list.
  • ← Download downloads the selected remote entries; double-clicking a remote file downloads it; you can also drag remote entries onto the local list.
  • Existing remote files are overwritten after a confirmation.

The Transfers list shows every transfer with its progress, size and result; Clear finished removes the finished ones.

Resuming: when a transfer fails (e.g. the connection was lost), ↻ Resume next to it continues where it stopped – a download keeps the part already received and asks the server only for the rest, an upload continues after the part the server already has. When you upload a file and a smaller file of the same name is on the server, the client asks whether to resume the upload; when you download into a local folder that contains a smaller file of the same name, it asks whether to resume the download. Resuming works with SFTP and with FTP servers that support REST and APPE (almost all do).

Comparing and synchronizing folders

With a local folder open (Chrome/Edge on the desktop) and a connection, ⇄ Compare / synchronize compares the local folder with the current remote folder, including all subfolders. The list shows every file that differs: only local, only on the server, local is newer, server is newer or different size (when the times do not tell which is newer), with size and modification time on both sides; Show identical files adds the files that are the same.

Every file gets an action – upload, download or skip – that you can change. Direction proposes the actions: both ways (the newer file wins), upload only (makes the server match the local folder) or download only. Synchronize puts the transfers into the queue; missing folders are created. Files are never deleted.

Files with the same size count as identical; tick Compare modification times when the sizes are equal to compare their times as well. Uploads keep the local modification time on the server (FTP MFMT, SFTP), so they count as identical afterwards. A browser cannot set the time of a downloaded file: downloaded files get the current time, which is why the comparison relies on the sizes by default. At most 5000 files per side are compared.

Managing remote files

New folder, Rename (one selected entry) and Delete (selected entries; folders are deleted with their content after a confirmation).

Open with… opens the selected remote file in another application of the suite; saving there uploads it again (shown in the transfer queue). With several files selected (Ctrl+click), the text editor or the hex editor opens all of them in one window, each in its own tab.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

Help

Keys Function
F1 / ? show this list (outside of text fields)

On phones and tablets

The lists are shown one below the other; ☰ Sites opens the saved sites.
